pq60mx9.s: Casual Italian restaurant on East 77th Street and one of the best date spots on the Upper East Side.

puuyq2s.s: Italian restaurant on Hester Street in Little Italy.

p1g35gfa.s: East Village sibling of Greenpoint's beloved Taqueria Ramirez, serving meltingly good, no-frills carnitas tacos.

p170ks9r.s: Sceney Dimes Square restaurant with bright red floors, faux-marble columns and satisfying Italian food.

pmdsr87.s: Cute Greenpoint wine bar for a catch-up or a date, with mushroom toast on She Wolf bread.

p1rrigf2.s: Cantonese fishballs and noodles on Bayard Street, from a Chinatown food cart that became a shop.

p1t15q7s.s: Chef Charles Gabriel's pan-fried chicken. The North Carolina-born, James Beard-nominated cook is a Harlem legend. Get the cornbread.

p16vy3r7.s: Food hall and shops in the old National Biscuit Company factory, with floors of reliable eats right by the High Line.

p1qij1pg.s: 12-table Upper East Side French bistro from the Sushi Noz team: luxe charcuterie, a famously pricey roast chicken and serious desserts.

p1q2683j.s: Flushing hot pot palace spread over two and a half floors, called "the Disneyland of hot pot" by The Infatuation.

p13npzmz.s: Midtown Chinese barbecue where you pick skewers from the fridge and grill them yourself. A very fun group night.

p1s5m2yj.s: 24-hour Latin diner on 14th Street from chef Julian Medina, styled like a Havana luncheonette. Cheap and reliable at any hour.

p1i6iwi9.s: NoHo diner open since 1972 and an Adam Sandler favorite. Order the soup. It has been reported to be nearing its final days, so check before you go.

p10buy1d.s: Studio-apartment-sized all-day Japanese cafe on Suffolk Street: Napolitan spaghetti, karaage, fruit sandos on milk bread, curry, coffee and matcha.

p138gz2j.s: Pell Street Sichuan restaurant with more than 150 spicy, saucy dishes on the menu.

phvf9di.s: Old-time SoHo tavern on Prince Street where Bob Dylan drank in the '60s, now enjoying a sceney renaissance.

pjqmw7a.s: No-frills Chinatown counter on Mosco Street selling some of the cheapest potstickers in town.

p1ssqnuw.s: Upper East Side branch of Fumo, an Italian restaurant and pizzeria on Second Avenue.

p8bs91x.s: One of Manhattan's most storied steakhouses, in the Theater District since the Prohibition era, when it began as a speakeasy.

pa7794k.s: Big Cantonese banquet hall on East Broadway for dim sum with a group.

pj5tkep.s: Upper West Side hot dog and tropical drink stand at 72nd and Broadway, a piece of New York lore since 1973.

p19vh8a.s: Midtown East sushi classic, one of the first restaurants to introduce New Yorkers to sushi. Good for a business lunch.

p1vnflwb.s: The Williamsburg sequel to The Four Horsemen, with niche amari, interesting wine and seasonal Italian food.

p1ilckhq.s: Small, family-run Korean restaurant with a mom-and-pop feel, known for kimchi jjigae.

pz9ltyk.s: Egyptian fish market and restaurant in Astoria: point at the seafood you want and choose how it's cooked.

pwar8hq.s: Contemporary Italian restaurant in Gramercy from chef James Tracey.

p1gcbhft.s: Jean-Georges Vongerichten's flagship French restaurant at One Central Park West, still one of the city's top fine-dining rooms.

p1hmija7.s: The rebooted Jing Fong in Chinatown: a much smaller dim sum restaurant than the old 800-seat hall, but still great for a group.

p1r48t3v.s: Jean-Georges Vongerichten's intimate Upper East Side restaurant, his first in New York.

p2jwtpl.s: Greenpoint supermarket that does far more than groceries, with prepared foods and specialty goods.

p11nd509.s: Midwood sushi restaurant whose biweekly whole-tuna carving is one of the most fun sushi experiences in the city.

p1lwuz03.s: The Lower East Side's legendary Jewish deli, a slice of pure New York history. Get the pastrami.

p1h7azig.s: Packed, affordable Greek restaurant on Division Street with seafood, lamb and mezze.

pumry1l.s: Tiny Hester Street shop making great, cheap dumplings, run by the dumpling maker from the old Prosperity Dumplings.

p150sq1d.s: Lower East Side branch of the hyped Williamsburg Chinese restaurant: mock eel, wok-seared long dumplings and newer dishes.

p1fa4pzr.s: Williamsburg slice shop that sets the standard for a New York slice with Italian ingredients. Yes, you'll wait. Yes, it's worth it.

p1se9al7.s: Daniel Boulud's French bistro in FiDi, a reminder of why he became famous.

p6n0wb6.s: Daniel Boulud's grand restaurant inside One Vanderbilt, opened in 2021 with lush greenery and skyline views.

pgmt4ih.s: Murray Hill restaurant specializing in Shanghainese food, including soup dumplings.

p5moo1i.s: SoHo branch of Lucia Pizza, good for a quick slice at lunch.

p1qmmxox.s: Italian wood-fired steakhouse in NoMad with velvet banquettes, red wine and red meat.
